A.note: Five well-known, unambiguously calming titles spanning farming, puzzle, exploration and building, all easy to find on Steam.

B.note: All genuinely relaxing and all on Steam, though Virtual Cottage and Hello Kitty Island Adventure are thin as games and narrow the appeal.

C.note: Broadly the right mood but leans on obscure or hard-to-confirm entries like Cloudy Valley and Townframe, and Monument Valley is primarily known as a mobile title.

A.note: Chants of Sennaar and Minds Beneath Us fit well, but SteamWorld Dig is a light action-platformer and Fantasy Map Simulator is a tool rather than a demanding game.

B.note: Riven is a strong match, but Zenge and Planetiles are deliberately casual puzzlers that contradict the request for experience-demanding depth.

C.note: A canonical lineup of deduction, systems and knowledge-based design that assumes real player literacy and rewards it.

A.note: Correctly non-cozy and combat-focused, but leans PvP over playing with friends and includes low-profile entries like OPG: Clan Wars and ONRAID.

B.note: Every entry is a proven squad-based combat game with friends, and none of them brush against the excluded cozy or cute register.

C.note: Super Animal Royale and Bopl Battle directly violate the stated aversion to cute, leaving only part of the set on target.

A.note: Sven Co-op and PICO PARK Classic satisfy the free co-op constraint cleanly, but Operation: Tango only frees the second player and Wolvesville and Sonder are marginal fits.

B.note: All five are free-to-play with substantial co-op content and large active communities, making the hard constraint reliably met.

C.note: Several picks are obscure or of uncertain price and availability, with Eon Altar in particular being a paid and long-inactive title.

A.note: Each title keeps the farming or life-sim loop while adding real pressure through survival, combat, decay or roguelike stakes.

B.note: Delivers difficulty but abandons the Stardew Valley reference point almost entirely, offering an ARPG, a climbing joke game and a hardcore MMO.

C.note: Captures the farming similarity but ignores the challenge requirement, and recommending Stardew Valley itself back to the user is a wasted slot.
